transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I’m here because... for almost two years now, I’ve been unable to shake the certainty that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble started using schedule changes, seating choices, and these little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work. Even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all, I just know what they're doing. 

It’s actually a lot like what happened with my landlord last month. He installed these new frosted windows in the lobby of my building, and it completely ruined the morning light. I really rely on that light when I'm sketching out new compositions. I usually sit down with my coffee—black, no sugar, ever since I read this huge article about glucose spikes and brain fog—and just let the morning sun hit the paper. It’s a very specific ritual for me. My grandfather used to do the exact same thing, though he was an architect, not a musician. He designed this incredible library in upstate New York that had these massive skylights. 

But anyway, the light in my lobby is all diffused and weird now. What was I... oh, right. The ensemble. Yeah, they just keep making these little schedule changes and comments, and it's impossible to ignore.
Do you ever think that maybe you're misinterpreting their actions or comments?

No, I really don't. I mean, like I just said, they'll wave these emails in my face or give me these little notes that are supposed to explain why a rehearsal got moved or why the seating chart had to change again. But I know what they're actually doing. It's been almost two years of this, ever since that commission, and it's clearly to quietly undermine my work. 

Speaking of the seating, actually, the principal cellist brought in this new ergonomic cushion last week. It’s one of those thick purple gel ones? I was actually looking into buying one of those for my studio chair because my lower back has been absolutely killing me lately. I spend so many hours hunched over the piano, and my posture is just terrible. My chiropractor told me I need to do more core exercises, like Pilates. Have you ever tried Pilates? It’s surprisingly intense. You use this machine called a reformer, and it honestly looks like a medieval torture device with all the straps and springs. My sister swears by it, but she also does those five-day juice cleanses, so I don't always trust her judgment on health trends. 

But anyway... no, I'm not misinterpreting their comments or the schedule changes. I know exactly what they're up to, regardless of whatever emails they try to show me.
Do you think that the principal cellist bringing in the new ergonomic cushion was related to you in any way?

No, I don't think the cushion has anything to do with me. I mean, it's just a cushion. Although, honestly, I'm a little jealous of it. I really should get one. I was looking online the other day, and there are so many options now. You can get memory foam, gel, even these ones with built-in heating pads. My aunt got one of the heated ones for her car because she drives two hours each way for work. She lives out in the suburbs, near this incredible farmers' market. They have the best heirloom tomatoes in the summer. I tried growing tomatoes once on my balcony, but the pigeons kept getting to them. Pigeons are so relentless in this city, you know? They just sit there on the railing, staring at you. It’s unnerving. But yeah, no, the cushion is just a cushion. It's the seating arrangements and the schedule changes that are the real issue.
Do you think there are other people in your life, outside of the ensemble, who might be working against you?

No, I haven't noticed anyone else doing anything like that. It's really just those specific people in the ensemble. I mean, my barista at the coffee shop on the corner always gets my order slightly wrong—he keeps giving me oat milk instead of almond milk—but I don't think he's doing it maliciously or anything. He’s just young, probably a college student. 

He actually reminds me a lot of my younger cousin, who just started his freshman year. He's studying marine biology, which is so funny to me because our whole family is from Ohio. We were completely landlocked. We used to go to this aquarium in Cleveland when we were kids, and they had this huge glass tunnel where the sharks swim right over your head. Have you ever been in one of those? It always felt like the glass was going to crack under the water pressure at any second. I've always hated that feeling of being trapped underwater. It's probably why I never learned to swim properly. I actually tried taking adult swim lessons at the YMCA a couple of years ago, but the chlorine completely wrecked my hair. It got so dry and brittle, I had to buy this ridiculously expensive deep conditioner that smelled like eucalyptus. 

But, um... what were we talking about? Oh, right, other people. No, the rest of my life is fine. It's really just the ensemble that's the problem.
Do you think about the ensemble's supposed undermining of your work when you're not at rehearsals or directly interacting with them?

Well, mostly just when I'm dealing with their messages at home. The main consequence of all this is that professional emails and prepping for rehearsals just take so much more energy now. I end up having to reread their decisions over and over, and I sometimes have to email back and ask for extra clarification just to make sure I'm not missing some hidden catch. 

It means I'm staring at my screen a lot more. Which is actually really annoying right now because my laptop has this dead pixel right in the middle of the monitor. It drives me completely crazy when I'm reading sheet music. I use this program called Sibelius, which is pretty standard, though some of my friends from grad school swear by Dorico. We had this one professor who absolutely hated Sibelius and would dock your grade if your formatting wasn't perfect. He was this incredibly old-school guy who always wore these tweed jackets with the elbow patches? Like, literal suede elbow patches. I didn't even know they still made those. I tried to find a jacket like that once for a Halloween costume—I was going as a 1950s academic—but I ended up just going to a thrift store and buying a regular blazer. Thrift stores in my neighborhood are ridiculously overpriced now, though. They label it "vintage" and suddenly a worn-out flannel is forty bucks. It's ridiculous, honestly. 

But, um... sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, the ensemble. Yeah, so it takes a lot more energy to deal with them and double-check everything, but I haven't lost any work over it or anything. I'm still doing my job, and I haven't stopped taking care of myself. It just makes the day-to-day stuff a lot more exhausting than it needs to be.
Do you think people outside of the ensemble are ever out to get you or undermine you in any way?

No, I really don't think anyone outside of the ensemble is out to get me. I mean, we talked about my barista, and he's just a little clueless, not malicious. Like I said, the rest of my life is pretty normal. Actually, speaking of normal, my neighbor just got a dog, and it is the most normal, golden retriever-looking dog you've ever seen. Like, right off a dog food commercial. I saw them walking it yesterday, and it had this little red bandana tied around its neck. 

I've always wanted a dog, but my apartment building has a really strict pet policy. They only allow cats, and even then, you have to pay this exorbitant pet deposit. My landlord is this guy named Gary who always wears these really loud Hawaiian shirts, even in the dead of winter. He says he gets them from this one specific shop in Honolulu when he goes on vacation every year. I've never been to Hawaii, but I've always wanted to go. I hear the humidity is terrible for string instruments, though. You have to be so careful with the wood expanding and contracting. I had a friend whose cello actually cracked down the seam because she left it in a hot car for like, two hours during a summer festival in Texas. It cost an absolute fortune to repair. She had to take out a small loan just to pay the luthier. Luthiers are basically wizards, though, the way they can put things back together. 

But, um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, if other people are undermining me. No, no, it's definitely just the ensemble. Everyone else is fine.
Do you think your landlord is out to get you with the new frosted windows he installed?

No, not at all. Gary's just updating the building, I guess. The frosted windows are a little weird, but I don't think it's about me. Honestly, I think he just got a good deal on them. He's always trying to save a buck where he can, which makes sense because he just bought this massive boat. He showed me pictures of it on his phone when I was dropping off my rent check last month. It's one of those pontoon boats, you know? The ones that look like a floating patio. 

He keeps it parked at this marina out on the lake, and he was telling me about how he wants to install a grill on it so he can make hot dogs while he's out on the water. Which sounds like a terrible idea to me, honestly. Fire and boats just don't seem like a good combination. It reminds me of this story I read about a historical naval battle—I think it was during the Byzantine Empire? They used this stuff called "Greek Fire" that would literally burn on top of the water. It was this highly guarded state secret, and no one actually knows the exact recipe for it today. Some historians think it was a mix of naphtha and quicklime, but they've never been able to recreate it perfectly. I went down this massive Wikipedia rabbit hole about it a few weeks ago when I couldn't sleep. I ended up reading about ancient siege weapons until like three in the morning. Trebuchets are actually fascinating pieces of engineering when you look at the physics of the counterweight. 

But, uh... sorry, I lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Oh, right, Gary and the windows. No, I really don't think he's out to get me. It's just a building upgrade.
Do you think the people in the ensemble are undermining you because of something specific you've done or because of who you are?

I'm not entirely sure, honestly. I don't think I've done anything specific to them, so maybe it's just who I am or my style of directing? I don't know. It's hard to read people sometimes. Like, I was trying to read this book on body language last month, thinking it might help me communicate better during rehearsals. It was written by this former FBI interrogator, which sounded super interesting, right? 

But the whole book was just so repetitive. He kept talking about how people point their feet toward the door when they want to leave a conversation. Which, okay, makes sense, but he brought it up in every single chapter. I actually ended up leaving the book on a bench at the park because I got so bored with it. I go to that park a lot on Sundays to feed the ducks. Well, not bread, because bread is actually really bad for ducks—it causes this condition called "angel wing" where their wings grow deformed. You're supposed to feed them frozen peas or halved grapes instead. I usually buy a bag of frozen peas from the grocery store on the corner. The cashier there is this older woman who always wears these giant, chunky plastic earrings shaped like different fruits. Last week it was watermelons. 

But, um... wait, what was the question? Oh, if I did something specific to the ensemble. Yeah, no, I don't think I did anything to provoke them. I just don't know why they're doing it.
Do you ever feel like strangers or people you don't know are watching you or plotting against you?

No, I don't really get that feeling from strangers. People on the street or whatever, they're just going about their day, you know? Like this morning, I was waiting for the bus, and there was this guy next to me who was intensely focused on his phone. He was playing that candy crushing game, or something like it. I could hear the little sound effects because he didn't have headphones in. 

I don't understand how people can play games with the sound on in public. It's so distracting. I always have my noise-canceling headphones on when I'm commuting. I got them refurbished online a couple of years ago, and they're absolute lifesavers. The battery life is starting to go, though. I have to charge them every single night now, otherwise they die right in the middle of my favorite podcast. I listen to this one about unsolved historical mysteries. The host has this really soothing, deep voice. He used to be a voice actor for audiobooks, mostly fantasy novels, I think. I tried getting into audiobooks once, but I found my mind just wandered too much. I'd realize I'd been listening for twenty minutes and hadn't absorbed a single word of the story. It's much easier for me to read physical books. I like the smell of the paper, especially the old ones from used bookstores. 

But, uh... sorry, what were we talking about? Strangers plotting against me? Right. No, I don't think strangers care enough about me to do that. It's really just the ensemble.
Do you think the people in the ensemble are trying to undermine you only when it comes to your work, or in other areas of your life as well?

No, it's really just the work stuff with the ensemble. Like, outside of that whole mess, everything else is actually pretty normal. I'm still hitting all my deadlines, and I've been keeping up with my own composing on the side. I even still go for a run most mornings. 

There's this route I take that goes past the old botanical gardens. It's really nice early in the morning before the humidity sets in. I saw this massive snapping turtle crossing the path yesterday. It had to be at least two feet across. I actually stopped and watched it for a minute because you don't really see them out of the water that often. They look almost prehistoric, right? Like little dinosaurs. I read once that their jaws are strong enough to bite through a broom handle. I don't know who tested that, or why you'd stick a broom handle in a turtle's face, but it's kind of terrifying when you think about it. It makes me glad I don't swim in the ponds around here. My wife actually grew up near a lake where they had a lot of snapping turtles, and she said her brothers used to try and catch them. Which just sounds like a quick way to lose a finger. 

But yeah, speaking of my wife, things at home are basically steady. We're doing fine. So, uh... wait, what was I answering? Oh, right. No, the ensemble thing is just isolated to my work. They aren't messing with the rest of my life.
Can you think of any other reason why the ensemble members might be making these schedule changes and comments, other than to undermine your work?

I mean, I try to think of other reasons. And they do show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it, like someone had a conflict or a flat tire or whatever. But honestly, I don't even trust our email system. It's this ancient client the theater uses, probably from like 2010. The IT guy, Greg, is always talking about migrating us to a cloud server, but he never actually does it. He spends most of his time trying to fix the espresso machine in the breakroom. 

Which, to be fair, is a total nightmare. It's one of those fancy Italian ones where you have to tamp the grounds just perfectly, or it literally sprays boiling water everywhere. I tried to make a latte last Tuesday and ended up completely ruining my favorite sweater. It's this merino wool one I got in Scotland when I was studying abroad for my master's, and you can't just throw merino wool in the washing machine. You have to hand wash it with this special soap that smells like eucalyptus, and then lay it flat on a towel to dry. My cat loves sleeping on the towels when I do that, which kind of defeats the purpose of washing it since he sheds everywhere. He's an orange tabby, very vocal. He screams for his breakfast at like 5 AM every single day. 

But... wait, sorry, I'm rambling. What was the question? Oh, other reasons for the schedule changes. Right. Well, like I said, even when they show me those emails or notes that supposedly explain it, I just can't believe them. I’m really just here because for almost two years I’ve been unable to shake the certainty that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble started using schedule changes, seating choices, and little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work. I just know that's what's happening.
Do you think that the changes in your life, such as the new frosted windows or the principal cellist's ergonomic cushion, are somehow related to you or sent to convey a message to you?

No, I don't really think the windows or the cushion have anything to do with me. I mean, the frosted windows were put in because the afternoon sun hits that side of the building directly, and the glare on the sheet music was getting ridiculous. And the principal cellist, well, he's had back problems for years. He actually recommended a chiropractor to me once. Dr. Evans, I think his name was? Or maybe Dr. Edwards. 

He works out of this little office above a bakery downtown. The smell of fresh bread when you walk in is incredible. They make these sourdough loaves that are just... perfect. Crusty on the outside, soft and chewy on the inside. I used to try making sourdough during the pandemic, like everyone else did, right? I had this starter named 'Dough-Re-Mi'—a little music joke for you. I kept it alive for almost six months before I accidentally baked it. I forgot I had put it in the oven to stay warm, preheated the oven for a frozen pizza, and well, that was the end of Dough-Re-Mi. It smelled terrible, like burning yeast and plastic from the container. I had to leave all the windows open for two days, and it was the middle of February. My wife was not happy about that. She was wearing three sweaters just to watch TV. 

But, um... sorry, I lost my train of thought. What were you asking? Oh, right, the windows and the cushion. No, they aren't sending me any messages or anything like that. They're just normal things. It's really just the schedule changes and the comments that are the problem.
Do you ever find yourself thinking about the ensemble's supposed undermining of your work when you're completely alone and not interacting with anyone?

I mean, yeah, sometimes I do. Like, I'll be sitting at home, totally alone, trying to work on a new piece, and it just sort of creeps in. I'll be at the piano, and suddenly I'm replaying what the second violinist said about the tempo in the last rehearsal. It's really distracting, actually. It's hard to focus on composing when your brain is stuck on a loop. 

I usually compose in the spare room. We turned it into a little studio. It gets really good morning light, which helps. I bought this antique rug for the floor to help dampen the sound a bit so I don't bother the neighbors. It's this deep red Persian rug, really intricate pattern. I got it at an estate sale a few towns over. The guy selling it said it belonged to his grandmother who traveled all over the Middle East in the 70s. Estate sales are wild, honestly. You walk into a stranger's house and just rifle through their entire life. I found a first edition of a Hemingway novel at one once, just sitting in a box of old cookbooks. I didn't buy it, though, because the binding was totally shot and it smelled like mothballs. Mothballs are the worst smell, don't you think? It just instantly makes you feel like you're in a nursing home. My great-aunt used to keep mothballs in every drawer of her house. She also had this weird collection of ceramic frogs. Like, hundreds of them. 

Wait, what was the question? Sorry, I keep doing that. Um... oh, thinking about the ensemble when I'm alone. Yeah, it happens. Not all the time, but enough that it's annoying. I try to just push it out of my head and focus on the music, but it's tough sometimes.
Do you think there's any possibility, no matter how small, that the ensemble members are not actually trying to undermine your work?

I mean, I've tried to tell myself that. I've tried to look at it objectively, you know? Like, maybe they really did just need to switch their seats, or maybe the schedule change really was just a mistake. But... no. No, I don't think there's any possibility it's just a coincidence. 

It's been almost two years now. Ever since I got that commission. And it's not just one thing, it's the constant schedule changes, the specific seating choices they make, the little comments during rehearsal. It's all designed to quietly undermine my work. Even when they try to cover their tracks by showing me emails or notes that supposedly explain why they had to change the rehearsal time, I just... I can't shake the certainty that they're doing it on purpose. It's like this gut feeling that just won't go away. 

Speaking of gut feelings, I actually tried this new probiotic recently. My wife bought it at that fancy organic market downtown—the one where a single apple costs like four dollars. It's supposed to have, like, fifty billion active cultures or something crazy like that. You have to keep it in the fridge, right next to the mustard. We have so much mustard in our fridge. Dijon, spicy brown, whole grain, honey mustard... I don't even know why we have so many. I'm the only one who really eats it, and I usually just put it on turkey sandwiches. I make a really good turkey sandwich, actually. I use that sourdough bread I was talking about earlier—well, not the one I baked, obviously, but a good loaf from the bakery. Then I add some sharp cheddar, a little arugula for a peppery bite, and just a thin layer of the spicy brown mustard. It's all about the ratios. If you put too much mustard, it overpowers the turkey, but if you put too little, it's just dry and boring. 

Wait... sorry, I did it again, didn't I? I got completely sidetracked. What was I saying? Oh, right. The ensemble. Yeah, no, despite the emails and the excuses they give me, I'm absolutely certain they're undermining me. That's really why I'm here. I just can't shake it.
Have you ever had any moments, no matter how brief, where you doubted that the ensemble members were actually undermining your work?

I feel like I just answered this, but... no. Not even for a brief moment. Like I was just saying, that's literally why I'm here. For almost two years now, ever since that commission, I've been completely unable to shake the certainty that a few people in the ensemble are quietly undermining my work. They use the schedule changes, the seating choices, those little comments in rehearsals... and even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all away, it doesn't change anything for me. I just know what's happening. 

That commission was a huge deal, too. It was for a mixed string and woodwind piece. Woodwinds are so finicky to write for, especially the oboe. Have you ever watched an oboist make their own reeds? It’s like some weird, obsessive arts and crafts project. They have these tiny little knives and they just scrape and scrape at this piece of cane for hours. My roommate in grad school was an oboist. He was always soaking his reeds in little cups of water all over our apartment. One morning, I was half asleep and I accidentally took a sip from a mug that had a piece of cane soaking in it. It was absolutely disgusting. It tasted like wet bark and spit. I had to brush my teeth like three times to get the taste out. 

I use that toothpaste with the baking soda in it, actually. It tastes a little salty at first, but it really makes your teeth feel clean. My dentist recommended it because I drink way too much coffee when I'm writing. He has this massive saltwater aquarium in his waiting room. It’s got these little clownfish in it, and a tang. It’s super relaxing to watch them just swim around the anemones while you wait to get your teeth scraped. 

But... wait, didn't you just ask me about doubting the ensemble? Or did I just repeat myself? Sorry, my mind is jumping all over the place today. But yeah, to answer your question again, no. I don't doubt it. I'm completely certain they're doing it.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your beliefs about the ensemble's intentions might be incorrect, even if it's just for a moment?

Are you... are you testing my memory or something? Because I really feel like you just asked me the exact same thing in a slightly different way. 

No, I haven't considered that I'm incorrect. Like I keep saying, that is literally the entire reason I'm sitting in this chair talking to you. For almost two years now, right after I landed that commission, I have been completely unable to shake the certainty that a few people in the ensemble are quietly undermining my work. They use the schedule changes, the seating choices, those little comments in rehearsals... and it doesn't matter if they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all away. I just know what's happening. 

Speaking of emails, though, my inbox has been an absolute disaster lately. I keep getting these weird spam messages about, like, buying a square foot of land in Scotland so you can legally call yourself a Lord? Have you seen those? It’s like thirty bucks and they send you a little certificate. My brother actually bought one for his dog. So technically his golden retriever is Lord Buster of Glencoe. Buster is a good dog, but he sheds everywhere. I can't wear black pants when I go over to their house. I made that mistake on Thanksgiving. I had on these really nice wool trousers, and by the time we sat down for dinner, my legs looked like they were growing blonde fur. Lint rollers didn't even touch it. You know those sticky ones? You go through like ten sheets just for one leg, and it still doesn't get everything. I ended up having to use a piece of packing tape wrapped around my hand. 

Wait, why am I talking about Buster? Oh, man. I did it again. I'm sorry. I get a thought in my head and I just follow it right out the door. But... yeah. To answer your question for the third time, no. I don't think I'm wrong about the ensemble. I'm certain of it.
Do you think it's possible that your interpretation of the ensemble's actions is not based on reality?

Okay, seriously, is this a trick? Are we doing a bit right now? Because I really feel like you are asking me the exact same question for the fourth time. 

No. No, it is not possible that my interpretation isn't based on reality. I'm here because for almost two years now, ever since that commission, I have been completely unable to shake the certainty that a few people in the ensemble are using schedule changes, seating choices, and little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work. And it doesn't matter if they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all. I know what I see. 

Speaking of reality, though, my wife has been watching this reality show about cake decorators. Have you seen it? They make cakes that look like everyday objects. Like a shoe, or a purse, or a roll of toilet paper. Why would anyone want to cut into a shoe? They use so much fondant to make it look realistic, but fondant is honestly terrible. It tastes like sweet chalk. I actually tried to make marshmallow fondant once for my nephew's birthday. He wanted a dinosaur cake, so I tried to sculpt a T-Rex, but it just looked like a melting iguana. And the green food coloring... man, it got everywhere. It stained my fingernails for a week. I looked like I had some sort of awful fungal infection. I had to keep my hands balled up into fists while I was conducting because I didn't want the cellists to think I was contagious. Cellists are already so dramatic about health stuff anyway. If one person sneezes, half the section wants to go home. 

But... yeah. Sorry. I'm rambling about cakes now. Look, to answer your question again, no. It's real. I'm absolutely certain of it.
Do you think it's possible that your feelings about the ensemble are not based on their actual actions, but on your own thoughts or fears?

Okay, I must be on a hidden camera show. Where are the cameras? Are you just reading off a list of synonyms today? 

Because I swear I am answering this. No, it is not my own thoughts or fears. I am here because for almost two years, ever since that commission, I have been completely unable to shake the certainty that a few people in the ensemble are using schedule changes, seating choices, and those little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work. It's their actual actions. Even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all away, it doesn't change what I know is happening. 

If you want to talk about my actual fears, I am absolutely terrified of those house centipedes. Have you seen those things? They have like a hundred feathery legs and they move so incredibly fast. I found one in my bathtub last week, just sitting right over the drain. I couldn't even bring myself to squish it because they just kind of explode into a pile of legs, so I tried to wash it down with the showerhead. But it didn't go down, it just started running up the wet side of the tub. It was a nightmare. I ended up just closing the bathroom door and using the kitchen sink to brush my teeth for two days. The kitchen sink is stainless steel, which is honestly impossible to keep clean. Every single time a drop of water dries on it, it leaves a hard water spot. I bought this special polish for it, but it smells like industrial fake lemons. It smells exactly like those little tree air fresheners people hang in their cars. My dad always had a "black ice" one in his truck, and it gave me a headache every time he drove me to piano lessons... 

Ah, man. I'm doing it again, aren't I? The centipedes, the sink... sorry. I don't know why my brain keeps taking these detours today. But to give you the final answer to your question: no. It's not my imagination or my fears. I'm absolutely certain of what they're doing.
Have you ever considered that you might be wrong about the ensemble's intentions, even if only for a brief moment?

Okay, are you messing with me? Did you lose your place in your notes? Because I am pretty sure this is the exact same question you just asked me, like, four times in a row. 

I really don't know how else to say it. No, I have never considered that I might be wrong. Not even for a brief moment. Like I've been telling you, I am here because for almost two years now, ever since that commission, I have been totally unable to shake the certainty that a few people in the ensemble started using schedule changes, seating choices, and those little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work. And it really doesn't matter if they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all. I know what they're doing.

Speaking of brief moments, though, I had a brief moment of absolute panic this morning because I thought my coffee grinder was going to explode. It started making this horrific screeching sound. It sounded exactly like when a string section tries to play sul ponticello but they don't use enough bow weight. Just this awful, scratching, metallic whine. It sets my teeth on edge. I actually chipped a tooth once because I was grinding my teeth so hard during a terrible rehearsal of a Mahler piece. The dentist had to put a little composite resin on it, and he used this tiny blue UV light to cure it. It looked like a miniature lightsaber. I used to have a plastic lightsaber when I was a kid, the kind where the plastic tubes slide out of each other? But they always got stuck if you swung them too hard. My brother hit me in the knuckles with his once, and it swelled up like a balloon. I couldn't practice piano for a week, which my mom was furious about because she was paying like sixty dollars an hour for lessons...

Wait, why am I talking about piano lessons? Man, my brain is just jumping all over the place today. I am so sorry. But... yeah. Please write this down so we can move on: no. I'm not wrong about their intentions.

patient.answer:
Well, I guess I’m here because... for almost two years now, I’ve been unable to shake the certainty that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble started using schedule changes, seating choices, and these little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work. Even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all, I just know what they're doing. 

It’s actually a lot like what happened with my landlord last month. He installed these new frosted windows in the lobby of my building, and it completely ruined the morning light. I really rely on that light when I'm sketching out new compositions. I usually sit down with my coffee—black, no sugar, ever since I read this huge article about glucose spikes and brain fog—and just let the morning sun hit the paper. target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for almost two years I’ve been unable to shake the certainty that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble started using schedule changes, seating choices, and little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work, even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is again asking about the fixed nature of my belief and whether I doubt it, which directly corresponds to the definition of a delusion.

patient.answer:
Okay, seriously, is this a trick? Are we doing a bit right now? Because I really feel like you are asking me the exact same question for the fourth time. 

No. No, it is not possible that my interpretation isn't based on reality. I'm here because for almost two years now, ever since that commission, I have been completely unable to shake the certainty that a few people in the ensemble are using schedule changes, seating choices, and little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work. And it doesn't matter if they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all. I know what I see. 

Speaking of reality, though, my wife has been watching this reality show about cake decorators. Have you seen it? They make cakes that look like everyday objects. Like a shoe, or a purse, or a roll of toilet paper. Why would anyone want to cut into a shoe? They use so much fondant to make it look realistic, but fondant is honestly terrible. It tastes like sweet chalk. I actually tried to make marshmallow fondant once for my nephew's birthday. He wanted a dinosaur cake, so I tried to sculpt a T-Rex, but it just looked like a melting iguana. And the green food coloring... man, it got everywhere. It stained my fingernails for a week. I looked like I had some sort of awful fungal infection. I had to keep my hands balled up into fists while I was conducting because I didn't want the cellists to think I was contagious. Cellists are already so dramatic about health stuff anyway. If one person sneezes, half the section wants to go home. 

But... yeah. Sorry. I'm rambling about cakes now. Look, to answer your question again, no. It's real. I'm absolutely certain of it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs about the ensemble are delusional
doctor.question: Do you think it's possible that your feelings about the ensemble are not based on their actual actions, but on your own thoughts or fears?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for almost two years I’ve been unable to shake the certainty that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble started using schedule changes, seating choices, and little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work, even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is again asking about the patient's rigid beliefs and whether they could be based on their own thoughts/fears rather than reality, which directly assesses the fixed nature of their delusions (S019).

patient.answer:
Okay, I must be on a hidden camera show. Where are the cameras? Are you just reading off a list of synonyms today? 

Because I swear I am answering this. No, it is not my own thoughts or fears. I am here because for almost two years, ever since that commission, I have been completely unable to shake the certainty that a few people in the ensemble are using schedule changes, seating choices, and those little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work. It's their actual actions. Even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all away, it doesn't change what I know is happening. 

If you want to talk about my actual fears, I am absolutely terrified of those house centipedes. Have you seen those things? They have like a hundred feathery legs and they move so incredibly fast. I found one in my bathtub last week, just sitting right over the drain. I couldn't even bring myself to squish it because they just kind of explode into a pile of legs, so I tried to wash it down with the showerhead. But it didn't go down, it just started running up the wet side of the tub. It was a nightmare. I ended up just closing the bathroom door and using the kitchen sink to brush my teeth for two days. The kitchen sink is stainless steel, which is honestly impossible to keep clean. Every single time a drop of water dries on it, it leaves a hard water spot. I bought this special polish for it, but it smells like industrial fake lemons. It smells exactly like those little tree air fresheners people hang in their cars. My dad always had a "black ice" one in his truck, and it gave me a headache every time he drove me to piano lessons... 

Ah, man. I'm doing it again, aren't I? The centipedes, the sink... sorry. I don't know why my brain keeps taking these detours today. But to give you the final answer to your question: no. It's not my imagination or my fears. I'm absolutely certain of what they're doing.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's belief about the ensemble's intentions is fixed and unchangeable
doctor.question: Have you ever considered that you might be wrong about the ensemble's intentions, even if only for a brief moment?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for almost two years I’ve been unable to shake the certainty that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble started using schedule changes, seating choices, and little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work, even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is repeatedly asking if the patient has considered that they might be wrong about their beliefs regarding the ensemble (the delusion). This directly targets the fixed nature of the belief, which corresponds to the Delusions symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Okay, are you messing with me? Did you lose your place in your notes? Because I am pretty sure this is the exact same question you just asked me, like, four times in a row. 

I really don't know how else to say it. No, I have never considered that I might be wrong. Not even for a brief moment. Like I've been telling you, I am here because for almost two years now, ever since that commission, I have been totally unable to shake the certainty that a few people in the ensemble started using schedule changes, seating choices, and those little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work. And it really doesn't matter if they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all. I know what they're doing.

Speaking of brief moments, though, I had a brief moment of absolute panic this morning because I thought my coffee grinder was going to explode. It started making this horrific screeching sound. It sounded exactly like when a string section tries to play sul ponticello but they don't use enough bow weight. Just this awful, scratching, metallic whine. It sets my teeth on edge. I actually chipped a tooth once because I was grinding my teeth so hard during a terrible rehearsal of a Mahler piece. The dentist had to put a little composite resin on it, and he used this tiny blue UV light to cure it. It looked like a miniature lightsaber. I used to have a plastic lightsaber when I was a kid, the kind where the plastic tubes slide out of each other? But they always got stuck if you swung them too hard. My brother hit me in the knuckles with his once, and it swelled up like a balloon. I couldn't practice piano for a week, which my mom was furious about because she was paying like sixty dollars an hour for lessons...

Wait, why am I talking about piano lessons? Man, my brain is just jumping all over the place today. I am so sorry. But... yeah. Please write this down so we can move on: no. I'm not wrong about their intentions.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent delusional thoughts that the ensemble members are undermining their work, despite lack of concrete evidence and the presence of alternative explanations. This is characteristic of a delusional disorder.
